analysis: Integration of 10 unit analyses. Supplied changes are docs (changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md; docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 3 and 252-260; docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md lines 3 and 784-791; docs/developer/test.md ~177-216; docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md line 3 and row at 119), a libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (14661d9->c17693f), and a new opt-in live test, ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift. The docs describe a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import that builds destinations from zeroed host buffers and skips eval and stream fences, so SSD restore staging no longer waits on MLX's process-wide evalLock. The import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. The doc row says the zero source can briefly commit memory outside the MLX allocator. The test is gated by DARKBLOOM_RESTORE_CONTENTION_BENCHMARK=1 and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_EXCLUSIVE_GPU=1, uses per-condition cache scopes, writes a timing report with no prompt content or keys, and adds no production surface. Threats considered: T-041 (SSD cache, SEC-035), TB-007, T-028, T-010, T-029, T-016. The visible evidence does not change DBK3 AES-GCM, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping, the 30-minute TTL, the KEK or the coordinator boundaries. No finding is supported. The actual code (the submodule diff, CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift) was not supplied, so these points are unverified: (1) the scratch charge is enforced through GlobalKVCacheBudget/ProcessMemoryLedger before allocation, since memory outside the MLX allocator is a possible availability gap; (2) destinations are fully overwritten only after authenticated decrypt, and failed restores never expose zeros or stale data as a valid prefix; (3) there is no read-before-fill race once fences are skipped; (4) staging reservation release paths are unchanged. Because the submodule diff is invisible, deeper review is recommended.
